# Environmental Engineering (BS)

---

The program requires a minimum of 130 units.

- BISC 220Lg General Biology: Cell Biology and Physiology Units: 4 *

## Major Requirements

---

### Engineering

---

- ENGR 102 Viterbi First-Year Academy Units: 2

### Civil and Environmental Engineering

---

- CE 108 Programming for Civil and Environmental Engineers Units: 2
- CE 110 Introduction to Environmental Engineering Units: 2
- CE 119 Statistical Data Analysis in Engineering Units: 2
- CE 215 Statics and Dynamics Units: 4
- CE 309 Fluid Mechanics Units: 4
- CE 330 Computational Methods in Engineering Units: 2
- CE 363L Environmental Chemistry and Analysis Units: 4
- CE 408 Risk and Decision Analysis in Civil Engineering Units: 2
- CE 410L Environmental Engineering Microbiology Units: 4
- CE 451 Water Resources and Coastal Engineering Units: 4
- CE 483 Engineering Economics in Civil Engineering Units: 2
- CE 485 Water and Wastewater Treatment Design Units: 4
- ENE 200 Environmental Engineering Principles Units: 4
- ENE 215 Energy Systems and Environmental Tradeoffs Units: 4
- ENE 300 Contaminant Transport in the Environment Units: 4
- ENE 415 Environmental Organic Chemistry Units: 4
- ENE 428 Air Pollution Fundamentals Units: 4

### Design Courses

---

Choose one design course (4 units) from the following list:

- CE 450 Coastal Engineering and Design Units: 4
- Or
- CE 476 Design of Hydraulic Systems Units: 4

### Other Requirements

---

- CHE 330 Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics Units: 4

### Advanced Computing

---

Students who must take MATH 125g Calculus I will be waived from the required Advanced Computing course.

notes.text: The program requires a minimum of 130 units. A cumulative grade point average of C (2.0) is required for all courses taken at USC as well as all upper-division courses applied toward the major, regardless of the department in which the courses are taken. In addition, a minimum grade of C must be earned in the following course: ENE 410 . See also common requirements for undergraduate degrees .
